cc.t: The American Society of Transplantation had one job when the government unveiled a kidney plan.
Speak for the people waiting.
Instead, it put out a statement.
No target. No deadline. No dollar amount. No role for patients.
Read the statement twice. Then look at who the AST is built for.
Start with the door.
To join, you pay.
Doctoral membership is listed at four hundred eighty-five dollars a year.
Membership is built around people who work in transplantation.
Being a patient is not on the list.
In twenty twenty-five, it opened an affiliate tier for people in industry with a business or strategic interest in transplantation.
Corporate partners are invited to meet with the board every year, to discuss strategy.
Patients get a toolkit, and a link to register as a donor.
The Living Donor Circle of Excellence is the society's showpiece for living donation.
Its members are companies. Its founding member is UnitedHealth Group, an insurer.
Patients are the subject of the program. They are never members of it.
Now the board.
To be nominated, the society's own criteria have asked for five years of membership in good standing, attendance at its meetings, a record of leadership inside it, and two letters of reference.
Five years of dues and meetings, just to be considered.
No patient. No care partner.
That is not a board patients can reach. It is a board that stays inside the club.
Follow the structure.
Dues in. Meetings. Industry at the table. Patients at the edge, holding a toolkit.
In twenty twenty, this society wrote that for-profit organizations inherently are incentivized to prolong dialysis over offering transplantation.
Those are its words.
Now apply that test to the AST.
The federal plan sets direction. It sets no rules, and no deadlines.
A society that put patients first would demand both.
This one issued a statement.
So here is what we demand.
Patients and care partners on the board, with full votes.
Nominations open to people outside the dues-paying club.
A public account of every dollar it takes from industry.
And dated, public targets for the outcomes it claims to care about.
This is not leadership.
It is public relations.
And we have buried too many people to keep pretending otherwise.
